definition: Moral outsourcing is the placing of responsibility for ethical decision-making onto external entities, often algorithms.
details: The term is often used in discussions of computer science and algorithmic fairness, but it can apply to any situation in which one appeals to outside agents in order to absolve themselves of responsibility for their actions. In this context, moral outsourcing specifically refers to the tendency of society to blame technology, rather than its creators or users, for any harm it may cause.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. Think of it this way: Moral outsourcing is the placing of responsibility for ethical decision-making onto external entities, often algorithms. And here is the clever part: The term is often used in discussions of computer science and algorithmic fairness, but it can apply to any situation in which one appeals to outside agents in order to absolve themselves of responsibility for their actions. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” And that is Moral outsourcing — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
